title: Automotive Electrical Systems and Diagnosis
author: Erudior
description: Compare starters, alternators, converters, batteries, relays and networked controls. Build a protected harness, measure a fault and verify the repair. Includes a parts atlas and an assessed modification workshop.
changelog: Added two in-depth cases, four assessed questions, two study cards and a practical evidence record. A labeled circuit and voltage-drop record that locates one physical fault.

lessons.title: Follow the complete current path
lessons.body:
Entry skills: complete Workshop Measurement and Vehicle Service, or demonstrate the equivalent workshop skills.

A working load needs a path from the source through protection and a switch, through the load, and back to the source. Voltage is measured between two nodes. A connection can show continuity with the circuit off yet drop most of the supply voltage under load. Sketch the loop and choose the two exact nodes for each measurement.

## Worked shop case

A 12.0 V source supplies a 6 ohm resistive trainer. Ideal current is voltage divided by resistance, or 2 A. An incandescent lamp has temperature-dependent resistance, so use its operating rating to plan the real load.

## Guided practice

An ideal 12 V resistive circuit has 8 ohms total. Predict current in amperes.

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

**What you will produce.** A labeled circuit, physical harness and healthy/faulted/restored measurement log.

Identify individual components in the parts atlas and trace their interfaces on your exact donor drawing.

lessons.title: Starter circuits, alternators, batteries and converters
topics: Starter circuits, alternators, batteries and converters
lessons.body:
A starter solenoid switches a heavy load and may also engage the pinion. A conventional alternator rectifies generated AC for the DC bus. A smart charging system can vary its commanded voltage with load, temperature and battery state. Flooded lead-acid and AGM batteries can require different test and charging settings. Obtain the rated capacity, cold cranking specification, terminal orientation, restraint and applicable replacement procedure.

A mild hybrid can use a belt starter-generator and separate voltage domains joined by a DC/DC converter. A battery-electric car often maintains its low-voltage bus through a converter supplied by the traction system. A weak auxiliary battery can prevent systems from booting even with a charged traction pack. Trace power, return and command as separate paths. Keep live work on the fused, current-limited low-voltage trainer. Identify higher-energy systems from service information with their covers closed.

## Worked shop case

A fused teaching lamp draws 4 A. A measured 0.8 V drop across a connector under load implies 0.2 Ω and 3.2 W lost there. The circuit may show nearly full supply voltage on a high-impedance meter with the lamp disconnected. Loading turns the hidden resistance into a measurable loss.

## Guided practice

```example fade=2
problem: A 3 A trainer has a 0.6 V drop on its return. Calculate the return resistance.
step: Use the measured drop across the return.
step: Divide volts by amperes.
answer: 0.2 Ω; repeat under the same load after correcting the connection.
```

## Independent shop or design task

Trace a conventional starter/alternator layout and a donor with a DC/DC converter. Mark the source of low-voltage power, protection, return and wake request. On your fused trainer, measure actual healthy and faulted voltage drops.

Record the selected component, alternative, source and measured result in your component record. Identify open items for the design or practical reviewer.

lessons.title: Switches, relays, solid-state drivers, CAN and LIN
topics: Switches, relays, solid-state drivers, CAN and LIN
lessons.body:
A mechanical relay separates the coil command from load contacts. A solid-state driver switches with transistors, may regulate by pulse-width modulation and may report overload or open-load faults. A fuse protects its specified conductor circuit against excessive current. Changing the fuse size to mask a fault can leave the wire unprotected. Choose wire, terminal, protection, routing and seals as an assembly using applicable design data.

Distributed controls separate a driver's request from actuation. In one architecture a door module reads the switch, a body module receives a network message, and a motor driver feeds the window. High-speed CAN commonly uses a differential pair and LIN a single signal wire with a schedule controlled by a master node. Gateways can bridge networks. Connector appearance identifies neither protocol nor pin function. Start with topology, module power/grounds, network status and a trusted wiring diagram.

## Worked shop case

A scan tool sees the door switch change and the body module reports receiving the command. The window motor stays still. The evidence supports moving downstream to the output enable, driver protection, harness, motor and mechanism. Replacing the input switch would repeat a test already passed.

## Guided practice

```example fade=2
problem: A relay clicks and the lamp stays dark. What did the click establish?
step: It supports mechanical movement of the relay armature.
step: It cannot establish continuity through loaded contacts or the lamp return.
answer: Compare coil command, loaded contact drop and lamp supply/return on a protected trainer.
```

## Independent shop or design task

Draw a relay-switched version and a module-driven version of one accessory. On a low-current trainer compare control and load sides, label protection and demonstrate one diagnosed open connection.

Record the selected component, alternative, source and measured result in your component record. Identify open items for the design or practical reviewer.

lessons.title: Place protection and service test points
lessons.body:
Draw the supply, protective device, switch, lamp and return before cutting wire. Place source protection close to the supply and choose it with the trainer manufacturer's conductor and load ratings. Black-box components need named pins, polarity and connection labels. A lamp can have an accessible power point and a separate return test point.

## Worked shop case

A rated 12 W load at 12 V draws about 1 A at its working point. This identifies the running load. Final fuse and conductor selection also needs inrush, conductor rating, connector rating and supplier guidance.

## Guided practice

Two 6 W branches at 12 V are powered together. Predict the combined nominal current in amperes.

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## Your design

For a 12 V lamp of your choice, identify operating current from its rating. Draw and label protection, disconnect, return, meter points and expected healthy readings. Document supplier limits and specify a fault that a trainer can introduce safely.

```assignment
writing: design
```

## Component design review

Compare the candidates in the component register and bring your selected configuration into this design.

```assignment
writing: component-selection
```

Read a modification card, choose a baseline and identify the changed parts, including hardware and seals.

lessons.title: Budget voltage drop on the supply and return
topics: Budget voltage drop on the supply and return
lessons.body:
Draw battery positive, protection, switch or relay, load and return as a continuous loop. A small series resistance can be invisible to an unloaded meter. Under load that same resistance develops a voltage drop and dissipates heat. Separate the feed path from the return path. Avoid putting an ammeter directly across a power source. Perform the exercise on the course’s fused, current-limited low-voltage lamp trainer.

**Worked circuit.** A training supply provides 12.4 V under load. The positive path drops 0.5 V and the return drops 0.7 V. The load should see 11.2 V. At 2 A, 0.7 V across a return segment means 0.35 ohm and 1.4 W in that segment. Compare the drop to the known-good condition and equipment limits. The highest absolute voltage you see is not necessarily across the faulty segment. Place the probes at its two ends with the lamp operating.

**Design your test.** Draw a relay-fed accessory with serviceable test points at the source, each end of its contacts and the load return. Show the fuse protecting the selected conductor, including any smaller downstream branch. Choose ratings from the component data and actual current, wire length, temperature and routing. Predict how a poor positive connection and a poor return would change the four measurements.

lessons.title: Assemble and fault-find a 12 V trainer
lessons.body:
De-energize before crimping or moving connectors. Use the specified terminals and crimp tool, check conductor capture and secure the harness. With power off, inspect continuity and check for unintended paths. Use a fused, current-limited trainer. Select DC volts and the voltage jacks before taking a reading across two powered nodes.

## Worked shop case

Source 12.1 V, lamp 9.0 V, and return drop 0.1 V leaves roughly 3.0 V on the feed path. Break that path into smaller segments under the same load to localize the loss.

## Guided practice

A 12.0 V source, 10.5 V at the lamp terminals and 0.2 V on the return leave how many volts on the feed path?

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## US rules at the workbench

For covered workplace servicing where unexpected energization could injure workers, assess energy sources and apply the employer's energy-control procedure under 29 CFR 1910.147 where applicable. For this trainer, isolate and verify the source before changing wiring. A disconnected 12 V battery does not establish a safe traction-voltage condition in a hybrid. Document the meter, reference node and isolation boundary.

[OSHA — control of hazardous energy, 29 CFR 1910.147](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.147) · [OSHA — PPE, 29 CFR 1910.132](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.132) · [US DOE — maintenance and safety of electric vehicles](https://afdc.energy.gov/vehicles/electric-maintenance)

## Workshop preparation

Use a low-voltage instructional source. Keep leads in the voltage jacks for powered tests. Isolate power before changing wiring. Exclude vehicle battery, airbag and high-voltage circuits.

```assignment
lab: workshop
```

Bring the selected component record to the lab and enter what you personally inspected, made, measured or assembled, with the part identifier and actual conditions.

lessons.title: From accessory load to a serviceable harness
topics: From accessory load to a serviceable harness
lessons.body:
Open the parts atlas for this system. Trace a parent assembly into its named children and mounting hardware. Explain the function of each item, identify its controlling dimensions or interfaces, then decide which pieces you can machine or fabricate, which you can assemble and which to obtain as qualified assemblies. Put exact drawing or donor references beside your decision.

## Parts on the bench

Supply, wiring and body electronics, Additional body controls. The quick references linked below include the function, design, fabrication or installation route, and verification of every indexed item.

## Modifications to evaluate

- Auxiliary fused circuit and relay
- Amplifier, speakers and subwoofer
- Auxiliary data display or head unit with retained climate controls

## Worked example

A 4 A lamp circuit has 0.08 Ω total supply-and-return resistance under load. Its predicted drop is 0.32 V. If the measured current remains 4 A, an unplanned 0.10 Ω splice adds another 0.40 V and dissipates 1.6 W there. Inspect that connection before changing a lamp or upsizing a fuse.

## Guided decision

```example fade=1
problem: A loaded 2 A tester shows 0.4 V across one terminal. How much power is lost there?
step: Multiply the measured drop by load current.
answer: 0.8 W at the terminal; compare the drop again after the connection is corrected.
```

## Independent workshop

Build the fused low-voltage lamp project in the bench plans. Identify every terminal and protective item, compare baseline and changed configuration and attach the measured drops.

Open a modification card for its design, build and test sequence. Record original and changed readings under comparable conditions. Separate physical evidence from predictions and document a safe rollback.

```assignment
writing: modification-record
```

lessons.title: Find a hidden connection loss with the lamp operating
topics: Find a hidden connection loss with the lamp operating
lessons.body:
Mark each measurement node before energizing the protected trainer. Measure source voltage at its terminals, voltage directly across the lamp and the drops along each side. The three measured differences around the circuit should approximately balance under the same load. If the readings were taken across different conditions, repeat them before attributing the error to the harness.

**Worked fault.** The lamp dims. The source remains 12.2 V, the lamp has 9.8 V, and the total return drop is 0.1 V. About 2.3 V is missing on the feed side. Measure from the source to relay input, then across the closed contacts and from relay output to lamp feed. If the large drop is across a connector, isolate the supply before inspecting the terminals. An unloaded continuity beep after unplugging it cannot demonstrate performance at 2 A.

**Independent work.** Have another person select a documented fault insert rated for the trainer. Predict the side from the first measurements, divide that side into segments and identify the first excessive drop. Remove power, restore the circuit and repeat the readings at the same load. Explain how an added light bar, longer return lead or different grounding point would change the design calculation.

```assignment
lab: case-record
```

lessons.title: Verify a repair at the original load
lessons.body:
A lamp lighting up is a coarse check. Recreate the original load and repeat the same voltage-drop measurements with the same reference points. Record a small remaining drop with the meter resolution. If the fault remains intermittent, identify what condition is missing before replacing another part.

## Worked shop case

A switch lost 1.6 V before terminal replacement and 0.1 V after. Source voltage stayed steady under the same load. The measured improvement across that segment is 1.5 V.

## Guided practice

A connection lost 2.1 V before repair and 0.2 V afterward. Give the improvement in volts.

Predict the result, then use the first quiz item to check your reasoning.

## Practical sign-off

The faulted segment is identified from loaded readings and verified by a matched retest. Record actual measurements and the disposition of faults. Submit the physical evidence in the workshop record.

```assignment
lab: workshop
```

Close each build-relevant component row with its measured result, reviewer disposition or an identified open issue and retest. Transfer the accepted configuration to your capstone record.

Reconcile required, issued, installed and verified quantities against the physical assembly and mark unresolved items.

references.title: Component register and build evidence
references.body:
For this course examine Starter and flywheel drive; Charging and auxiliary battery; Harness, protection and switching; Body controls and communications; Instruments and warning indicators. Document manufacturer, part revision, drawing, selection, applicable authority or service requirement, installer, measured result with units, and reviewer disposition. Begin in design and update after installation.

| Family | Candidate designs | What changes | What to verify |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Starter and flywheel drive | Conventional solenoid starter / integrated starter-generator | Engagement method, current path and controller interlocks differ. | Trace supply and return on the correct diagram and measure the protected trainer under load. |
| Charging and auxiliary battery | Alternator / DC-DC; flooded lead-acid / AGM | Storage, regulation, terminal layout and charging strategy must match. | Record source mode, applicable test settings and load conditions. |
| Harness, protection and switching | Relay / solid-state driver; fuse / fusible link | Control and load paths differ. Protection must match the conductor and environment. | Draw a branch and record normal and faulted voltage drops on the fused trainer. |
| Body controls and communications | Direct switch / LIN node / CAN module with gateway | A received request and a powered actuator are separate facts. | Trace one request to a named downstream data point and then to its load. |
| Instruments and warning indicators | Discrete gauge or lamp / networked cluster | Changing a sender or controller can change scale, warning logic and diagnostic visibility. | Check units, plausibility and telltale operation against donor data. |

references.body:
For an actual vehicle, identify the exact model, part revision, operating conditions and source before using a specification. Course examples are teaching fixtures. Document the physical work you perform, your inspection measurements and any specialist operations. Preserve relevant emissions controls, required safety equipment and diagnostic functions. Determine requirements for the specific intended use and jurisdiction before committing to changes.

Use the parts identity record and the service procedure for the exact donor. EPA's federal tampering and defeat-device provisions can apply to emissions-related hardware or software. Identify supporting compliance evidence for the exact configuration. In California, check the specific Executive Order and application where an exemption is relevant. A successful dyno pull, cleared fault code or ready monitor cannot establish permission. For road use confirm state and local rules for registration, equipment, noise and inspection with the responsible authority. Colorado is the program's worked state example. references.title: Supply, wiring and body electronics · Auxiliary battery to Voltage regulator
references.body:
For an actual vehicle, identify the exact model, part revision, operating conditions and source before using a specification. Course examples are teaching fixtures. Document the physical work you perform, your inspection measurements and any specialist operations. Preserve relevant emissions controls, required safety equipment and diagnostic functions. Determine requirements for the specific intended use and jurisdiction before committing to changes.

### Auxiliary battery

**Function.** Supplies low-voltage energy and stabilizes supply.

**Design.** Choose chemistry, capacity, cranking rating, venting and terminal position.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Secure in a reviewed tray, connect vent if required and initialize per donor.

**Verify.** Perform a chemistry-appropriate condition test and inspect retention.

### Battery hold-down

**Function.** Restrains the battery under vibration and vehicle loads.

**Design.** Design ears, load path, clearance from posts and corrosion protection.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fabricate a reviewed bracket or fit the matched donor clamp.

**Verify.** Verify retention and clearance from hood and cables.

### Positive cable

**Function.** Carries starter or distribution current.

**Design.** Calculate drop and conductor rating for length, duty, environment and protection.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Cut to measured route, fit correct crimped lugs and protect bulkhead crossings.

**Verify.** Measure loaded drop and inspect heat, strain and abrasion.

### Ground strap

**Function.** Provides a low-resistance return between moving assemblies.

**Design.** Choose flexible conductor, current capacity and clean attachment points.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit with movement allowance and protect joint after achieving contact.

**Verify.** Measure loaded voltage drop from case to return point.

### Starter motor

**Function.** Converts battery energy to cranking torque.

**Design.** Match direction, pinion, flywheel geometry and cranking duty.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit the specified unit and draw the connection and mounting interfaces.

**Verify.** Compare cranking voltage, current and shaft speed with donor data.

### Starter solenoid

**Function.** Engages the drive and/or switches high current.

**Design.** Match control voltage, terminal order and starter drive.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install matched solenoid or supplied starter assembly.

**Verify.** Check command, contact drop and pinion disengagement.

### Alternator

**Function.** Supplies electrical power while the engine turns.

**Design.** Match pulley ratio, output at operating speed and control protocol.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit aligned brackets and the specified wiring and drive.

**Verify.** Measure commanded and loaded output and inspect belt tracking.

### Voltage regulator

**Function.** Controls alternator field or output.

**Design.** Determine local versus ECU control and sensing reference.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Fit matched regulator or complete alternator and preserve sense circuit.

**Verify.** Compare commanded and actual voltage at stated load.

references.title: Supply, wiring and body electronics · Rectifier bridge to CAN gateway
references.body:
For an actual vehicle, identify the exact model, part revision, operating conditions and source before using a specification. Course examples are teaching fixtures. Document the physical work you perform, your inspection measurements and any specialist operations. Preserve relevant emissions controls, required safety equipment and diagnostic functions. Determine requirements for the specific intended use and jurisdiction before committing to changes.

### Rectifier bridge

**Function.** Converts alternator AC to DC.

**Design.** Match current, thermal capacity and internal alternator design.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Use a matched rectifier during an authorized alternator rebuild.

**Verify.** Verify ripple against service limits using the approved method.

### Fuse or fusible link

**Function.** Opens a faulted conductor circuit.

**Design.** Coordinate wire rating, fault current, time characteristic and environment.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Install specified protection at the documented supply location.

**Verify.** Verify rating, continuity and protection of downstream wiring.

### Relay

**Function.** Switches a load with a separate command circuit.

**Design.** Choose contact rating, pinout, coil polarity and suppression.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Build with a rated socket and properly terminated conductors.

**Verify.** Measure coil command and loaded contact drop.

### Bulkhead grommet

**Function.** Prevents a panel edge from cutting a cable.

**Design.** Match cutout, sheet thickness, cable size, heat and movement.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Deburr the hole and seat the grommet around the protected run.

**Verify.** Pull gently and inspect both sides for contact or a displaced lip.

### Connector and terminal

**Function.** Provide separable electrical connections.

**Design.** Select current rating, keying, conductor size, seals and terminal finish.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Use the named crimp tool, fit seals and engage secondary locks.

**Verify.** Inspect crimp geometry and perform specified retention and loaded tests.

**Function.** Transfers permitted data between vehicle networks.

**Design.** Match bus topology, protocol and module configuration.

**Function.** Drives the wiping mechanism and establishes park.

**Make, assemble or fit.** Mount securely, fuse the supply near its source and make a sound return.

references.title: How to account for every installed part
references.body:
# Build-specific parts reconciliation

The teaching atlas lists common light-vehicle parts and service assemblies across multiple architectures. A gasoline manual, a diesel automatic and a battery-electric car have different inventories. The as-built bill of materials establishes what **your particular car** contains, down to separately installed hardware. Start with the actual model year, market, engine, transmission, option codes and donor/source identity. Mark privacy-sensitive paperwork for private instructor review.

1. Make a system tree for the exact vehicle. Give each parent assembly an ID. Identify the source of every child from a dated OEM parts catalog or exploded figure, engineering drawing, kit packing list, supplier specification, harness diagram or direct teardown. A commercial catalog is good for identity and fitment. Use separate authoritative service data for torque, installation and test limits. For original parts, assign drawing numbers and revisions yourself.
2. Start a line in As-Built-BOM.csv for each **part at each installation position**, including each clip, washer, spacer, seal, terminal, retainer, ground strap, hose end, fluid charge, service label and replacement-only fastener. Split left/right, front/rear, orientation and hardware stack order; link each to its parent. A separate serialized component gets its own instance. Account for consumables retained on the finished part, e.g. coating or sealant by product, batch and measured or specified amount where applicable. Mark discarded assembly aids separately.
3. Tie every row to an approved configuration. Record exact part/revision, the number or amount required, received or made, installed and independently verified, with units. Compare numbers at that installation position; purchased spare stock belongs to inventory, not installed quantity. Add any part missing from the teaching atlas. Mark a nonapplicable teaching family with the architecture-specific reason. A missing source entry is an open item.
4. Distinguish **make** (original or drawing-controlled part), **assemble** (purchased parts you personally integrated), **buy** (approved component) and **specialist** (named service or operation). Record material, tooling, process, measured features or supplier documents and who inspected it. Document critical work before it is hidden. Preserve service access and replace-only rules.
5. For a sealed bought assembly with no serviceable internal list, identify its make, model, revision or serial where available, supplier and functional boundary. List every separately fitted connector, seal, mount and fastener. If the manufacturer publishes a serviceable breakdown or you rebuild it, expand the children you actually service. Leave inaccessible internal details marked as supplier-controlled. Do not dismantle restraint inflators or sealed traction assemblies for an inventory exercise.
6. Reconcile from both directions. Walk each drawing callout into the build ledger, then walk each real installed item back to a drawing, receipt, material record or revision. Have a second person inspect quantities, location, retention and test evidence. Mark each row accepted, absent by design, awaiting evidence, rework or spare. Release a function only when all its relevant rows and measured acceptance tests have passed. Record who accepted the change. The complete car still requires the existing witnessed commissioning demonstration and its intended-use approvals.

## Worked example

The SP-01 removable-plate fixture drawing calls for one plate and one fastener/washer stack at each of two identified positions. Its practice board supplies tapped holes. The separate example CSV includes eight rows. They identify the board, the plate, two labeled mounting positions as parent groups, and the two screws and two washers distributed under those groups. Parent groups carry no physical quantities. A missing right washer is an intentional open finding. Correct the installed count only after fitting the washer; update verified count only after reinspection. Accepting the measured board and plate as individual parts leaves fixture release on hold until the corrected right stack is verified. An unused spare remains a stock item.

## Graduation review

Turn in the assembly tree, marked exploded views, drawing revisions, actual bill of materials, inspection evidence, change records and final service schedule. Account for every called-out or observed item and every receiving/installation discrepancy. An instructor must be able to pick an item on the physical car, identify who made or fitted it, locate its source or released drawing, and see how it passed the appropriate acceptance check. A passing written exam cannot certify workmanship, registration, emissions compliance or crashworthiness.

references.title: Make a fused, removable lamp harness
references.body:
**Objective.** Build a serviceable low-voltage accessory branch and prove both circuit operation and conductor condition. Use a current-limited 12 V DC bench supply, a 12 V lamp rated approximately 3 W with insulated holder, a compatible switch, source-end fuse and holder, polarized connector, insulated copper wire, terminals and a meter. Use the workshop’s approved component ratings and current limit, including lamp inrush. Keep the vehicle battery disconnected from this bench exercise.

1. Draw source positive → source-side fuse → switch → connector → lamp → connector return → source negative. Assign connector pin numbers and mark positive/return on your sketch. Approximately 3 W at 12 V gives 0.25 A under rated steady-state operation. Use actual measured current for your results.
2. Establish a route on the board. Measure both legs including service slack. Select insulation, terminals, wire, switch and protection from their documented ratings and the lowest-rated downstream conductor/connection. Verify the fuse suits expected current and inrush. Record fuse identity and rating rationale.
3. De-energize the supply. Cut and label conductors. Strip to the terminal maker's length, crimp with the matching die, inspect the conductor and insulation crimps, and seat and lock each contact. Fit source protection close to the source. Secure the loom and isolate exposed conductor.
4. Before power, verify polarity, routing, switch action, and absence of an unintended supply-to-return short with the load disconnected. Reconnect the lamp, configure the bench current limit under supervision, energize and check expected operation. Measure current using a compatible meter configuration or the supply readout. Never place an ammeter directly across the source.
5. With load on, measure voltage across the supply path, the lamp, and the return path. Their sum should agree with measured source voltage within measurement uncertainty. For example, 0.08 + 11.86 + 0.06 = 12.00 V. Disconnect power, replace a deliberately prepared high-resistance connector fixture with a known-good connector, repeat and compare at matched current. Do not create a short to test the fuse.

**Fresh assignment.** Add a serviceable second connector to a new branch on the board. Predict the allowed drop from your design limits, build it, test under load and explain whether easier service meets the electrical target. Capture all contacts, housings, seals, source protection, clips and wires by location. A lit lamp alone earns no measurement credit.

writing.title: Component selection and evidence
writing.prompt: For this course examine Starter and flywheel drive; Charging and auxiliary battery; Harness, protection and switching; Body controls and communications; Instruments and warning indicators. Identify each applicable family on your own vehicle or donor and explain absent families. Use two identified alternatives for at least one consequential choice. Show the job each design performs, how its operating principle differs, one failure mode and a test that separates the alternatives. writing.title: Workshop record · From accessory load to a serviceable harness
writing.prompt: Build the fused low-voltage lamp project in the bench plans. Identify every terminal and protective item, compare baseline and changed configuration and attach the measured drops. State the goal, the baseline test, a controlled change, a potential adverse effect, comparable measured results, acceptance threshold and rollback. Include an attributable photograph, recorded direct observation or measurement.
